title: What is known about 1RB1RF_0RC0RE_0RD1RA_1LE0LA_1LB0LD_0RD---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RF_0RC0RE_0RD1RA_1LE0LA_1LB0LD_0RD---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The tape is a queue of blocks (01)^k with k mostly powers of 4; a cursor eats one block a copy at a time and rebuilds it four times larger at the right end (proved in Lean). The order in which blocks are fed is not understood yet.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 63,806 cells have been visited and 33,410 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.448).

claims.title: Tape structure
claims.text: The tape is a list of blocks (01)^k separated by the word 10 111. The exponents are mostly powers of 4: at 108 steps the list reads (left to right) 2, 4×3, 15, 16×20, 18, 67, 67, 131, 258, 16, 4096, 4096, 140; at 109 steps 4×328, 8, 16×21, 32, 64×26, 72, 268, 268, 524, 913, 121. The active end on the right turns blocks into blocks four times longer, a bouncer whose repeated word changes, much like a counter in base 4.

claims.title: The feeding rule
claims.text: Fd k m L = L (01)^k 1 (01)^m 1 F> 0^inf: one visit of the right end takes Fd (k+1) m L to Fd k (m+3) L in 6m+24 steps, for all k, m and every tape L; iterated, Fd (k+j) m L reaches Fd k (m+3j) L.

claims.title: A queue of blocks of size 4^j
claims.text: The tape is a list of blocks (01)^k separated by 10111, k mostly a power of 4 or twice one; cursors near the right end use up blocks one copy at a time and rebuild them four times larger at the end. A second, two-cursor rule (a block loses one copy per visit, the next gains four, the last loses one) is seen in the run.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Missing: the two-cursor rule in Lean and the global schedule of the queue; see Next steps in the README.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0RE_1RC0RA_0LD0LB_0LA1LE_1LC1LF_0LA--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 63,806 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: Blocks that are eaten one piece at a time and rebuilt four times larger
html: Write a for 01 and b for 10111. The tape is a list of blocks of a's separated by b's, and the block sizes are (mostly) powers of 4:

Near the right end a cursor (a lone 1 where a b would be) separates the block being eaten from the block being built. Every time the head reaches the right end, one 01 leaves the block on the left of the cursor and three join the block at the end (proved in Lean for blocks of any size):

<svg viewBox='0 0 560 110' role='img' aria-label='one copy leaves the block left of the cursor, three join the end block' style='width:100%;max-width:560px;height:auto;font:12px var(--mono)'><rect x='10' y='15' width='200' height='22' fill='var(--ink)'/><text x='110' y='30' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--bg)'>a^(k+1)</text><rect x='214' y='15' width='8' height='22' fill='var(--head)'/><rect x='226' y='15' width='120' height='22' fill='var(--accent)'/><text x='286' y='30' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--bg)'>a^m</text><rect x='10' y='70' width='188' height='22' fill='var(--ink)'/><text x='104' y='85' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--bg)'>a^k</text><rect x='202' y='70' width='8' height='22' fill='var(--head)'/><rect x='214' y='70' width='168' height='22' fill='var(--accent)'/><text x='298' y='85' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--bg)'>a^(m+3)</text></svg>

So a block of k copies is turned into about 4k copies at the end. The whole run behaves like a counter whose digits are how many blocks of each size there are. What is not understood yet is the schedule: which block is fed next and when a new cursor is created, so there is no closed rule from one stage to the next, and no answer about halting.

Where it could halt

Only when, in state A, the head reads a 1 and steps right onto another 1. In the run the head always comes to the right end on blank tape.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.448).
After 109 steps the tape spans 63,806 cells (1,022 left of the start, 49,939 right), with a density of 1s of 0.524.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: A queue of blocks (01)^k with k mostly powers of 4, eaten one copy at a time at a cursor and rebuilt four times larger at the right end, like a base-4 counter; the feeding rule is proved in Lean; open.
